title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods
venue: Academic Press (textbook; orig. 1982, Athena Scientific reissue 1996, this Academic Press/Elsevier edition 2014, ISBN 978-1-4832-3613-1)
conclusions: Comprehensive treatment of constrained optimization via Lagrange multiplier / dual methods, including augmented Lagrangian and sequential quadratic programming methods
Develops penalty-function approaches, duality theory, and exact (differentiable and nondifferentiable) penalty methods for equality- and inequality-constrained problems
Establishes the classical primal-dual / multiplier-update machinery (multiplier ascent under violation, convergence to KKT points) that underlies modern Lagrangian constrained-learning methods
Originally published 1982 (Academic Press); reissued 1996 by Athena Scientific; the cited edition is a 2014 Academic Press/Elsevier reprint of the original text (same content, ISBN 9781483236131)
Does not itself address deep learning, transductive prediction-count constraints, or soft/hard count mismatches -- it is the classical numerical-optimization foundation, not an ML paper
our_use: main.tex:150-153 -- 'Encoding requirements as constraints and solving with primal-dual methods is the classical recipe \citep{bertsekas2014constrained}, brought to deep networks by Lagrangian-duality training \citep{fioretto2020lagrangian} and given statistical footing by PAC constrained-learning theory...' -- cited purely as the classical/foundational reference for Lagrange-multiplier and primal-dual constrained-optimization methods, before pivoting to the deep-learning instantiations (Fioretto et al.) that our TraLO/dual-ascent baselines build on.
issues: none -- title, sole author, publisher and year all verified against authoritative sources (Bertsekas's own athenasc.com/MIT pages plus ScienceDirect/SciRP listings). The 2014 Academic Press/Elsevier entry is a legitimate distinct-ISBN edition of the same text (not a typo for 1982 or 1996); citing it with publisher='Academic Press' and year=2014 is internally consistent and matches that specific printing. Usage is a standard, unembellished background citation (classical recipe), no overclaim, correct \citep usage.
